questions.q: Name three different traditional Indian dishes from three different states mentioned in the chapter.
questions.a: Example: Biryani (Hyderabad), Dhokla (Gujarat), and Rosgulla (Bengal). A student who struggles here likely hasn't engaged with the regional examples provided in the text; remind them to visualize a map of India and assign one food to each major region.

questions.q: What does "unity in diversity" mean in the context of Indian society?
questions.a: It means that even though Indians have many different languages, religions, and customs, they are bound together by a shared identity and common history. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks diversity means "being divided" or "not belonging together," showing a lack of understanding of the "Many in the One" concept.

questions.q: If a student from Punjab moves to Tamil Nadu, how might their food and dress habits represent both diversity and unity?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify the student's original culture (e.g., eating makke di roti). 2. Identify the new environment's culture (e.g., eating idli/dosa). 3. Recognize that the student maintains their identity (diversity). 4. Recognize that both are part of the Indian diet (unity). A wrong answer reveals the student sees diversity as a "clash" rather than a "coexistence."

questions.q: Compare how festivals like Makara Sankranti are celebrated differently across India, yet represent the same underlying event.
questions.a: While the festival has different names (Pongal, Bihu, Lohri) and specific local customs, it is celebrated at the same time and marks the harvest season. A wrong answer reveals the student is focusing only on the labels rather than the shared purpose or timing of the event.

questions.q: Is cultural diversity a problem that makes a country weak? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, it is a strength because it enriches the country with different perspectives, arts, and traditions, creating a "Many in the One" structure. A wrong answer suggests the student believes uniformity (everyone being the same) is the only way to have a strong nation, missing the concept of enrichment.

questions.q: Design a hypothetical "Unity Festival" for your school that includes at least three different cultural elements from different parts of India.
questions.a: A good answer would include a specific regional food stall, a traditional dance performance, and a display of different regional textiles. A poor answer is generic or fails to link the activities to specific Indian regions, showing a lack of research into cultural variety.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Cultural diversity refers to the existence of a wide variety of customs, languages, foods, dresses, and festivals within a society, all ______ under a shared national identity.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are at a ______ station in India—what do you see?
What is Cultural diversity? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Cultural diversity refers to the existence of a wide variety of customs, languages, foods, dresses, and festivals within a society, all coexisting under a shared national identity.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Cultural diversity?
questions.a: Students often confuse "diversity" with "division." They believe that because people eat different foods or wear different clothes, they must be fundamentally different or unable to live together.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to categorize examples of food, dress, and festivals by region and explain how these differences coexist within the broader framework of Indian unity.
